rows.title: No Emmys For Films On TV If They're Eligible For Oscars
rows.standfirst: Feature films forced to premier on the small screen because of the coronavirus crisis will not compete with television shows for awards.

rows.title: Amtrak To Require Masks Starting Monday To Avoid Spread Of The Coronavirus
rows.standfirst: Customers will have to wear masks in stations, on trains and on Thruway buses. Amtrak is booking only half of each train's normal capacity, making it easier for passengers to sit farther apart.

rows.title: Grocery Worker Has Never Seen Shelves Being Emptied Like This
rows.standfirst: Michelle Lee, a Safeway cashier, wishes customers would be more patient about shortages. "They can't understand why they keep coming back and we don't have" items such as toilet paper, she says.

rows.title: Some Companies Are Turning To Tracking Technologies To Ensure Safe Reopening
rows.standfirst: Companies are trying to figure out how to welcome back employees to their offices, and keep them safe once they return. The new normal might involve smartphone apps and badges to track employees.

rows.title: Gov. Newsom On Reopening California
rows.standfirst: California Governor Gavin Newsom talks with Stacey Vanek Smith about his plans to reopen the fifth largest economy in the world.

rows.title: Table For None: Tom Colicchio Explains What Restaurants Need To Survive
rows.standfirst: The Top Chef judge is focused on keeping his industry afloat during the pandemic. "We're really looking at saving every restaurant, because we think that every restaurant needs to be there," he says.

rows.title: At The Frozen Pizza Factory That Never Closed: Social Distancing In A Tent
rows.standfirst: Carolyn Mendel oversees a team of about 1,000 people at a factory in Ohio that makes Totino's Pizza. A tent for employee breaks is among the safeguards added to protect the workers.

rows.title: FCC Fines Sinclair Record $48 Million For Deceptive Bid For Tribune Stations
rows.standfirst: FCC Chairman Ajit Pai called Sinclair's conduct "completely unacceptable" in pursuing Tribune Media. Sinclair has close ties to the Trump administration but received a record $48 million fine.

rows.title: Neiman Marcus Bankruptcy Is 1st By A Department Store During Coronavirus Crisis
rows.standfirst: The luxury chain known for its extravagant Christmas Book catalog had been losing money before the pandemic. The move follows J.Crew's bankruptcy filing on Monday, foreboding potentially more to come.

rows.title: 3.2 Million More Are Out Of Work As Jobless Claims Keep Piling Up
rows.standfirst: Another 3.2 million people filed for benefits, bringing the total number of jobs lost during the pandemic to 33.5 million. The government is expected to report a huge jump in unemployment Friday.

rows.title: Data Sharpen Focus On How Many Workers Lost Jobs To COVID-19
rows.standfirst: The number of people who have filed first-time claims for unemployment is updated Thursday. And on Friday, the government releases the April unemployment report.

rows.title: Georgia's Open Question
rows.standfirst: Can you safely reopen a business right now — and should you? | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Masks En Vogue
rows.standfirst: If the pandemic goes on much longer, or its aftereffects linger, face masks will inevitably become a fashion accessory.

rows.title: More Americans Are Getting Tested, But Experts Warn Of Second Wave
rows.standfirst: The White House Coronavirus Task Force is not disbanding, but instead shifting its focus to "opening up our country," according to President Trump.

rows.title: Facebook Oversight Board On Removing Objectionable Content Announces Members
rows.standfirst: The company has faced criticism in recent years for its handling of issues ranging from user privacy to policing hate speech to stopping the spread of disinformation.

rows.title: Restaurants Are Desperate — But You May Not Be Helping When You Use Delivery Apps
rows.standfirst: In a bid to help restaurants, cities from Seattle to Washington, D.C., have passed caps restricting how much food apps can charge to deliver meals. App companies claim the move might backfire.

rows.title: Reopening Sports: Does MMA Point The Way?
rows.standfirst: Mixed martial arts is the first major spectator sport in the U.S. to host live events since the coronavirus lockdown. Other sports are watching to see whether MMA could point the way.

rows.title: Delta To Retire 777 Fleet As Demand For Travel Plummets Amid Coronavirus
rows.standfirst: The wide-bodied planes were used for ultra-long-haul flights. It's a signal Delta does not anticipate international travel will pick up anytime soon.

rows.title: His New Amazon Warehouse Job Got Him Something He Really Wanted From His Previous Job
rows.standfirst: The hourly pay at Amazon is much lower than what Theodore Johnson earned as a massage therapist, but the new job comes with a key benefit he didn't have before.

rows.title: Wisconsin Bars Welcome Crowds After Court Strikes Down 'Safer At Home' Bans
rows.standfirst: One bar posted an image of a crowd, along with the caption: "45 minutes after the bars open in Wisconsin."

rows.title: Remdesivir Distribution Causes Confusion, Leaves Some Hospitals Empty-Handed
rows.standfirst: Gilead Sciences is donating its initial supply of the experimental treatment for COVID-19. The federal government is deciding where the scarce medicine goes, and there are questions about the choices.

rows.title: 36.5 Million Have Filed For Unemployment In 8 Weeks
rows.standfirst: Nearly 3 million people filed for unemployment benefits last week, the Labor Department says. It's the latest grim sign of the economic damage from the coronavirus crisis.

rows.title: Millions Of Pigs Will Be Euthanized As Pandemic Cripples Meatpacking Plants
rows.standfirst: As the pandemic wreaks havoc on the meat industry, hog farmers anticipate they'll soon be forced to euthanize millions of pigs unable to be sent for processing.

rows.title: The Restaurant From The Future
rows.standfirst: With over 5.5 million workers unemployed or furloughed, no other industry has been hit harder than restaurants. Yet one guy is thinking about expanding. Huh? | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Coronavirus Reset: How To Get Health Insurance Now
rows.standfirst: At least 27 million Americans who lost their jobs in recent weeks also lost their health insurance, a new report finds. Others lacked a health plan even before COVID-19 hit. Here's how to find help.

rows.title: 7-Year No-Interest Loans: What It Takes To Sell Cars In A Pandemic
rows.standfirst: U.S. new car sales have been recovering for six straight weeks. They're still low compared with pre-coronavirus levels, but huge incentives have helped attract buyers despite an economic crisis.

rows.title: Coronavirus, Farmworkers And America's Food Supply
rows.standfirst: The working conditions on many farms mean that agricultural laborers are at high risk of getting COVID-19. That poses a real threat to those workers and to the country's food supply.

rows.title: Uber Woos Grubhub, In A Move Lawmaker Calls 'Pandemic Profiteering'
rows.standfirst: The merger talks have yet to reach a deal, but if both sides strike an accord, the combined company would emerge as the dominant player in food delivery with 55% of the U.S. market.

rows.title: Apple, Google Coronavirus Tool Won't Track Your Location. That Worries Some States
rows.standfirst: Apple and Google are developing smartphone technology to help fight the coronavirus pandemic. But public health authorities in some states are chafing against the tech giants' rules.

rows.title: Fed Chief Says More Relief Spending May Be 'Costly, But Worth It'
rows.standfirst: Jerome Powell said the economy should recover once the coronavirus is under control. But the central bank chief cautioned that without more help, many small businesses may not survive that long.

rows.title: Florida Theme Parks Getting Ready To Reopen With Anti-Coronavirus Measures
rows.standfirst: Legoland and Universal have local approval for their plans, which involve taking temperatures and encouraging face masks. Disney World and SeaWorld haven't presented their plans yet.

rows.title: Face Masks Provide A New Frontier For Retailers During Coronavirus Crisis
rows.standfirst: Many popular brands including Nordstrom and Gap now sell nonmedical grade face masks to meet consumer demand, but experts say mask sales are a drop in the bucket compared to COVID-19-related losses.

rows.title: Waiting For A Surge
rows.standfirst: Hospitals lost millions of dollars preparing for a surge of COVID-19 patients. Some were swamped, but others only saw a handful of coronavirus cases. Now many are struggling to survive.

rows.title: How A Decades-Old Unemployment Insurance System Is Measuring Up In The Pandemic
rows.standfirst: Indivar Dutta-Gupta, a co-executive director at the Georgetown Center on Poverty and Inequality, explains the U.S. unemployment insurance system's origins and role today.

rows.title: Facebook Expects Half Its Employees To Work Remotely Permanently
rows.standfirst: CEO Mark Zuckerberg says he expects 50% of the social network's workforce to be working remotely within the next decade.

rows.title: New Zealand's Prime Minister Touts 4-Day Week To Boost Domestic Tourism
rows.standfirst: A shorter workweek to encourage travel? Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern says it's an idea worth considering as the island nation emerges from its coronavirus lockdown.

rows.title: Macy's Sees A $1.1 Billion Loss, While Pandemic Lifts 'Essential' Stores Like Walmart
rows.standfirst: Temporary store closures during the pandemic hammered nonessential retailers, including Kohl's, T.J. Maxx and Victoria's Secret. Shoppers also dramatically cut back on buying clothes.

rows.title: Getting An Antibody Test For The Coronavirus? Here's What It Won't Tell You
rows.standfirst: As more and more people get tested for antibodies to the coronavirus, infectious disease specialists worry that those tested — and their employers — may not understand the limits of the results.

rows.title: 'Between Life And Death': McDonald's Worker Says Pandemic Puts Safety In Focus
rows.standfirst: In his 30 years working at McDonald's, Bartolomé Perez joined several strikes to demand higher wages and better benefits. But the stakes have felt very different during the coronavirus pandemic.

rows.title: Congress could allow banks to charge higher overdraft fees. How to avoid extra costs
rows.standfirst: On Tuesday, the House is expected to vote on the resolution to lift the overdraft fee cap. A few simple tools can help you hold onto your hard-earned dollars.

rows.title: 38.6 Million Have Filed For Unemployment Since March
rows.standfirst: The United States is still losing jobs at an alarming pace two months after the coronavirus pandemic took hold. Another 2.4 million people filed claims for jobless benefits last week.

rows.title: There's Still Time To Get A (Remote) Summer Internship
rows.standfirst: Some companies are going virtual with their summer internship programs; other firms have simply canceled theirs. Here's our resource guide to finding the internships that are out there.

rows.title: Ideal Nursing Homes: Individual Rooms, Better Staffing, More Accountability
rows.standfirst: Nursing home experts say priorities need to change, emphasizing quality of life over profits. The stunning COVID-19 death toll brings scrutiny to an industry that many believe is due for an overhaul.

rows.title: She Gets Calls And Texts Meant For Elon Musk. Some Are Pretty Weird
rows.standfirst: Lyndsay Tucker, who works at a Sephora beauty store in San Jose, Calif., has tech billionaire Elon Musk's old cellphone number. So every day, she fields calls and texts intended for him.

rows.title: Researchers: Nearly Half Of Accounts Tweeting About Coronavirus Are Likely Bots
rows.standfirst: Researchers culled through more than 200 million tweets discussing the virus since January and found that about 45% were sent by accounts that behave more like computerized robots than humans.

rows.title: Target Says It Will Temporarily Close Stores In Several States As Protests Continue
rows.standfirst: The move comes after several Target stores were ransacked and damaged during protests.

rows.title: As Trump Targets Twitter's Legal Shield, Experts Have A Warning
rows.standfirst: Consensus is growing in Washington to repeal the decades-old law that protects tech platforms from lawsuits. Experts fear unintended consequences.

rows.title: As 'Hero' Pay Ends, Essential Workers Wonder What They Are Worth
rows.standfirst: Many retail and food workers are losing temporary wage bumps they got during the pandemic. Some say their work hazards are only increasing, while their wage is lower than unemployment benefits.

rows.title: Small America Vs. Big Internet
rows.standfirst: Small towns need fast internet. One town tried to solve the problem itself, but ran into a legal firewall. What gives? | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: The Beige Book And The Pig Farmer
rows.standfirst: The Federal Reserve's Beige Book provides anecdotes from various parts of the economy. This month's edition illustrates the pain being suffered by pig farmers.

rows.title: Trump, Retaliating Against Beijing, Revokes Privileges For Hong Kong
rows.standfirst: President Trump says the U.S. would take a number of steps after China's central government asserted more direct authority over Hong Kong, which it had pledged to treat differently.

rows.title: People Can't See It, But This Grocery Worker Still Wears Lipstick Under Her Mask
rows.standfirst: As a low-wage worker, Yesenia Ortiz wishes she would get paid more during the pandemic because of the extra level of risk to which she is exposed.

rows.title: Nick Hanauer: How Do We Begin To Reinvent Capitalism?
rows.standfirst: Billionaire entrepreneur Nick Hanauer says that today's inequality results from decades of bad economic theory. He argues for a reinvention of our capitalist system and our definition of prosperity.

rows.title: IRS Rule Shift Lets Workers Make Benefits Changes Midyear — If Their Employer Agrees
rows.standfirst: The new guidance amounts to a midyear open-enrollment period and applies to firms that buy health insurance to cover their workers as well as to those that self-insure — paying claims on their own.

rows.title: Theory Vs. Reality: Why Our Economic Behavior Isn't Always Rational
rows.standfirst: We don't always behave the way economic models say we will. We don't save enough for retirement. We give money to charity. This week, why we act in ways that go against our "rational" self-interest.

rows.title: 'The Sheer Volume' Is Hard To Capture: Unemployment In Nevada Soars To Historic High
rows.standfirst: Nearly 41% of jobs in the state's food and accommodation industry have been lost. The overall levels are comparable to the Great Depression, says David Schmidt, a state economist.

rows.title: Stung By Twitter, Trump Signs Executive Order To Weaken Social Media Companies
rows.standfirst: President Trump signs an executive order aimed at limiting the broad legal protections enjoyed by social media companies days after Twitter fact-checked two of his tweets.

rows.title: Melissa Dell On Security And Prosperity
rows.standfirst: Mellisa Dell, this year's John Bates Clark Medal winner, explains the relationship between security, prosperity and the rule of law.

rows.title: Frontline Workers Are Losing Temporary Wage Bumps Despite Increasing Risks
rows.standfirst: Many retail and food workers are losing temporary wage bumps they got during the pandemic. Some say their work hazards are still high, and their wage is lower than unemployment benefits.

rows.title: 'No Mask – No Entry,' Cuomo Says As He Allows Businesses To Insist On Face Coverings
rows.standfirst: "You don't want to wear a mask — fine," New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo says. "But you don't have a right to then go into that store if that store owner doesn't want you to."
